name: Essex Hall
summary: Essex Hall has long buff-brick residential wings turning around the entrance court, six visible levels broken up by shallow projecting window bays and pale masonry bands, and a lower wing extending behind the main block.

evidence.note: A dogleg west range, broad cross wing and long southeast range border the court. Lower pale roof behind the central range, rooftop service boxes along the elbow. Clean roof sample at local (69,1062).

Regional 2 m grid, heights above local ground. Median 18.31 m, P90 19.48 m, maximum 22.4 m. Main wings sample 18–20 m. The lower rear court-side volume samples 4–5 m. Tallest equipment and cores are about 22 m.
Long west range, repeated bedroom windows, bay projections and pale horizontal string courses.
Five rows over the glazed ground level face the forecourt. Paired narrow windows alternate with wider suites between full-height masonry piers. Buff brick sampled on the sunlit wall at (0.54,0.35).
The lower storey uses coarse masonry. Projecting stacked window bays have flat pale aprons. A short canopy protects the glazed entrance.
End wall seen from the drive is nearly blind in the middle and has projecting corner glazing.
North end steps up above the parapet with aerials above it, partially obscured from the intersection.
Entrance elevation shows stepped parapets at the vertical bays, tall slim stair windows, a rough faced plinth and a shallow canopy.
Housing lists six residential floors plus ground across the two wings. The entrance court photographs expose six window levels including the entrance level.

Frames 138541247 and 130394519 show two-window groups in the main south court facade, a rough masonry ground storey pierced by glazing and a shallow entrance canopy below the projecting left bay. The plinth is only the low projecting course.

Across the full western face of the southeast range, the last roughly eight metres of the elevation are uninterrupted brick. Windows turn the south corner. The closer oblique frame 130394513 confirms the blind end bay.

notes: Storeys describe exterior rows at the court. The ground level varies with the site. Selected bays project and wrap the corners. The detached green forecourt shelter has its own footprint w778714547. Paired condensers follow the west parapet beside the bedroom projections. Lidar over the south stair tower rises from about 18.3 to 21.2 m.
